prompt: The client asks: "Should we match a rival's 15% price cut?" Fact sheet: the rival cut prices 15%; we have lost 5% of volume in three months; our margin is 30%; a 15% cut would halve our profit per unit; analysts expect the category to grow 3% next year. Which is the best recommendation?

options.text: Match the cut. We've already lost 5% of volume in three months, and the losses will grow if customers see no response.
options.feedback: It ignores the deciding fact: a 15% cut halves profit per unit, so volume would have to double to break even.

options.text: Hold our price. At a 30% margin, a 15% cut halves profit per unit, so volume must double, and we've lost only 5%.
options.feedback: Right. It leads with the answer and backs it with the break-even math.

options.text: Don't match the cut. Analysts expect the category to grow 3% next year, so the lost volume will come back on its own.
options.feedback: Category growth doesn't decide this. The break-even math is what supports holding.

options.text: Matching protects volume and holding protects margin. The right answer becomes clearer after the next quarter.
options.feedback: This never commits, even though the math is clear.

explanation: Full answer: Don't match the price cut. With a 30% margin, a 15% cut halves profit per unit, so volume would have to double to break even; we've lost only 5% of volume. The main risk is that losses speed up, so the next step is to track share weekly and use targeted offers for the most price-sensitive customers. What would change the answer: volume losses heading toward half of sales.

irrelevant_facts: Analysts expect the category to grow 3% next year.
